_meta.role: Staff Software Engineer, Console GPU Inference

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY focused on GPU programming and machine learning inference performance. Wrote custom CUDA C++ convolution kernels (~35% faster than the naive GPU baseline through memory coalescing) and cut inference latency 5.2× with TensorRT. Built in C/C++ across embedded and GPU targets, with low-level profiling and 8-bit quantization for latency- and memory-constrained deployment.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 annotated images to 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for mobile inference deployment.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Trained U-Net segmentation with VGG-16, VGG-19, and ResNet-50 backbones (Dice, IoU) and reported accuracy-latency trade-offs; built the batch-loading pipeline for large 3D volumetric MRI inputs.
Led a team of 7 as team lead mid-project to deliver the full pipeline within the 6-week window.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Designed a custom wavelet bank (alpha-blended sym6+bior3.5) combined with optimized homography stitching and concurrency to reach PSNR 86 vs a 65 PSNR stitching baseline.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript conv layers in VGG16 with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights/biases, and preallocated global buffers to eliminate per-layer allocation overhead.
Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs 73.3ms (uncoalesced) and 77.5ms (CPU TorchScript) — ~35% speedup over naive GPU with identical classification accuracy.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated faster-whisper STT (1.0–1.4s), Gemini intent classification (<500ms), TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS vs eager PyTorch) for visual servoing, and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Built a LeRobot-structured data collection pipeline using multiprocessing for multi-camera frame capture.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory footprint by ~55% via 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled peak VRAM and inference latency across prompt types using pynvml and psutil.
Benchmarked across HellaSwag, GSM8K, and ARC; <1% accuracy degradation with +0.09 perplexity increase — near-lossless compression.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Implemented and benchmarked four parallel work distribution strategies (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) for rendering 5000×5000 pixel scenes using MPI.
Achieved up to 30× speedup with static strip partitioning (55 processes); demonstrated dynamic task queue outperformed all static methods under unpredictable workloads.
